In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electrical transport in in situ doped silicon nanowires is governed by the 3D VRH mechanism, which is consistent with the presence of a high density of tail states in the band gap of the nanowires.
the electrical transport in in situ doped silicon nanowires can be described by the variable range hopping mechanism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrical properties of the doped polycristalline silicon nanoribbons depend on the doping level and the type of dopant.
the conductivity of the polycrystALLine silicon nanowire is dominated by the hopping conduction mechanism.
the conductivity in in situ doped nanowires is dominated by variable range hopping conduction mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D VRH model is valid for a wide range of doping levels in N- and in P-type doped polycristalline silicon nanofibres.

the temperature dependence of conductivity of in situ doped silicon nanowires is well described by the variable range hopping model, and that the density of states is well described by an exponential (tail states).
